synopsis: A silly talking-game about a midnight job interview at a space station. No graphics, only dialogue, branches and state.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Good evening. I thought you were going to be late.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Welcome to Station 7, {player_name}! Night shift starts in seven minutes.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Great. Another interview at midnight. This station protocol makes no sense.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Quiet, Mira. {player_name}, I am Captain Rowan. Walk with me to the control room.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Don't worry, the captain sounds rough but he is polite when it matters.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: I am Professor Hale. I run the technical interview. Forty-two candidates failed it since 1998.
The corridor splits three ways. Where do you go?

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: The control room is behind the blue door. Mind the cables on the floor.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: The control room runs on an old API. It crashes if FPS drops below 30.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Station protocol, rule one: never touch the red lever. Ever.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Rule two: the night shift always shares its snacks. I brought cookies.
Sylvie offers you a cookie. Take it?

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Good choice! Sugar helps with the technical questions, {player_name}.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Wow. Declining free cookies. Bold interview strategy.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: You wish to know about me? I published 3.14 papers per year. Approximately.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: My field is station protocol engineering. The emergency channel is my design.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Translation: he wrote the manual nobody reads. It is 100% footnotes.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: The archive key opens every door here. Lose it, and you owe me seven favors.
The professor watches you. How do you respond?

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: Confidence. Good. The night shift needs people who say: I am ready.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Hey, it is fine. I said the same thing on my first night shift.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Leaving already? The exit is locked until the interview ends, {player_name}.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Classic. The door only opens for people with the archive key.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Come back inside. That was not a request. That was station protocol.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Sylvie is tired, but she smiles anyway. Follow me back, okay?

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: So. This whole night feels like a visual novel. Choices and everything.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Sylvie said she was ready hours ago. She is still waiting, poor thing.
The hall clock shows midnight. What now?

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: The board says: night shift briefing at 00:07 sharp. Do not be late.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: It also says the coffee machine achieved self-awareness in 1998. Avoid it.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: The archive key rests in locker number 7. The JSON manifest lists 42 items.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: I counted the lockers twice. There are {count} lockers on this floor!

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Your current score is [score], by the way. The station tracks everything.
Locker 7 is locked with an old HTTP panel. Try what?

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Zero zero zero zero? Really? Even the night shift deserves better hackers.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Fine. Mira sounded annoyed, but she typed something incredibly fast.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: The locker clicks open. Take the archive key, {player_name}.
The archive key glows faintly. What do you do?

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: Excellent. The archive key responds to polite holders only.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: It opens the emergency channel room. Professor Hale thanked her assistant.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Are you sure about all this? You look nervous, {player_name}.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: You are late for your own interview. Impressive record.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: I knew you would come back. Nobody leaves Station 7 on the first try.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Sylvie is tired. Carrying the night shift snacks is heavy work, you know?

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Captain Rowan told him to wait outside. Him, not you. Keep walking.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: Emotions are data. Tiredness means the night shift is working as designed.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Okay, serious question from the OpenAI fan club: is Qwen3 better at interviews?

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Do not listen to her. The manual is at https://example.com/station/alpha

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Enough chatter. The emergency channel just lit up. Move, all of you!

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Emergency! I repeat: this is not a drill, people!

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: The control room smells of ozone and old decisions. Forty-two lights blink red, then green, then red again, while the ancient ventilation system hums a low song that nobody remembers voting for, and I must admit the whole room feels like it is holding its breath waiting for someone competent to arrive.
Alarms everywhere. Your call?

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Good. Station protocol, page one: protect the archive key with your life.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Page two: hold my hand? No wait, that is just Sylvie being Sylvie. Sorry!
The alarm pattern changes. Respond?

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Wild improvisation! My favorite protocol. The night shift salutes you.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: It means the coffee machine woke up again. Or the station is doomed. Fifty-fifty.
Decide fast: the lights are failing.

choices.text: Grab the archive key and run.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: The emergency channel crackles. A voice older than Station 7 itself whispers seven numbers, then silence, then static, then a single polite cough that somehow contains more menace than the entire alarm system combined.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Did... did it just cough at us? Sylvie hides behind {player_name}.

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Steady. The night shift has survived worse. Probably. Maybe.

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Plot twist: it was the coffee machine all along. Told you. Night shift legend status: pending.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: You fixed the panel with 100% confidence and 0% understanding. Hired.
Dawn approaches. How do you end the night?

nodes.speaker: Captain Rowan
nodes.text: Welcome to Station 7, {player_name}. The night shift is yours.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: We did it! Cookies for everyone! Score: [score] points!
One last formality...

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: One more test? The interview never ends here. That is the station protocol.

nodes.speaker: Professor Hale
nodes.text: Clause 3.14: the signee agrees to love paperwork. Sign here: ______
The pen hovers over the paper.

nodes.speaker: Sylvie
nodes.text: Hired! Legend of the night shift! See you at 00:07, {player_name}!

nodes.speaker: Mira
nodes.text: Escorted out by Captain Rowan himself. Honestly? Worth it. 7/10 night.
